::: {#thm-r-squared-slr}
#### $R^2$ of a simple linear regression

For the OLS fit of a simple linear regression,
with $S_{xx} > 0$ and $S_{yy} > 0$,
$R^2 = r^2$,
where $r$ is the
[Pearson correlation coefficient](exploratory-descriptive.qmd#def-pearson-r)
of the $x_i$ and $y_i$.
In particular, $0 \le R^2 \le 1$.
:::

::: proof

With the notation of @thm-ols-slr,
the fitted values are $\hat{y}_i = \hintcoef + \hcoef{x} x_i$,
so each residual is

$$
\begin{aligned}
y_i - \hat{y}_i
&= y_i - (\bar{y} - \hcoef{x} \bar{x}) - \hcoef{x} x_i
&& \text{(substitute $\hintcoef$)}\\
&= (y_i - \bar{y}) - \hcoef{x} (x_i - \bar{x})
&& \text{(regroup)}
\end{aligned}
$$

Squaring and summing:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{i=1}^n (y_i - \hat{y}_i)^2
&= \sum_{i=1}^n \paren{(y_i - \bar{y})^2 - 2 \hcoef{x} (x_i - \bar{x})(y_i - \bar{y})
  + \hcoef{x}^2 (x_i - \bar{x})^2}
&& \text{(expand the square)}\\
&= S_{yy} - 2 \hcoef{x} S_{xy} + \hcoef{x}^2 S_{xx}
&& \text{(definitions of $S_{yy}$, $S_{xy}$, $S_{xx}$)}\\
&= S_{yy} - 2 \frac{S_{xy}^2}{S_{xx}} + \frac{S_{xy}^2}{S_{xx}}
&& \text{(substitute $\hcoef{x} = S_{xy} / S_{xx}$)}\\
&= S_{yy} - \frac{S_{xy}^2}{S_{xx}}
&& \text{(combine like terms)}
\end{aligned}
$$

The total sum of squares is $S_{yy}$, so:

$$
\begin{aligned}
R^2
&= 1 - \frac{S_{yy} - S_{xy}^2 / S_{xx}}{S_{yy}}
&& \text{(substitute into the definition of $R^2$)}\\
&= \frac{S_{xy}^2}{S_{xx} S_{yy}}
&& \text{(simplify)}\\
&= r^2
&& \text{($r = S_{xy} / \sqrt{S_{xx} S_{yy}}$)}
\end{aligned}
$$

Since $-1 \le r \le 1$
([range of the correlation coefficient](exploratory-descriptive.qmd#thm-pearson-r-range)),
$0 \le r^2 \le 1$.

:::
